author: zicokolter
text: Thank goodness SlidesLive is here to curate all our NeurIPS presentations.  It's clearly impossible to build some kind of "video hosting platform" where we could just post videos ourselves, without 8 weeks of lead time.

author: zicokolter
text: @tdietterich (And I’m annoyed they didn’t add chapters on convex/combinatorial optimization to the latest version … way more common in current AI conferences than many techniques covered extensively).

author: zicokolter
text: @tdietterich But I do actually feel like the one chapter Sasha was referencing doesn’t match up with current motivations for working in AI, this is all.

author: zicokolter
text: @tdietterich Perhaps people also interpreted my comment to mean we should replace AI with ML intros?  This is quite far from the truth, as evidenced by the actual AI courses I teach … I am perpetually annoyed by the frequent conflation of these terms in popular discussion.

author: zicokolter
text: @tdietterich Was being tongue in cheek, but naturally I fully agree. But considering a larger picture need not go hand and hand with the particular bigger picture painted by AIMA Chapter 2. I’ve always found it’s presentation rather disconnected from the diversity of motivations for AI.

author: zicokolter
text: Might you say that … a post-modern approach to AI is needed?  (the title of my last teaching statement, incidentally).

quoted.text:
Ill-Advised Rant: Despite working in AI for a decade, I find the introduction chapter in the AI textbook to be nearly alien language. 

(I hope this is not seen as punching down as this is one of the most popular CS texts in the world) /1 https://t.co/8I3oO1LrEE

author: zicokolter
text: Why exactly are we still having virtual conferences/workshops on weekends? There is no physical presence that makes a set of contiguous dates more convenient ... why not split workshops/conferences over separate weeks? We'd never expect seminars to be on weekends, why these?

author: zicokolter
zicokolter
text: New work with @priyald17 and @david_rolnick on efficient methods for training networks that integrate hard constraints and differentiable optimization!  To appear at #ICLR2021.

quoted.text:
Deep learning methods often struggle to satisfy hard constraints, limiting their practical use in domains such as power systems.

We tackle this challenge in our new #ICLR2021 paper on DL for approximate optimization:
https://t.co/bB9P7YHeQ2

w/ @david_rolnick & @zicokolter

1/ https://t.co/xGbiAnlFNC

author: zicokolter
text: Really excited about this new work with @deepcohen on the surprising properties of (full batch) gradient descent training of deep networks.  See thread (and you know ... the paper ... if you must) for details.

quoted.text: Our new ICLR paper demonstrates that when neural networks are trained using *full-batch* gradient descent: (1) the training dynamics obey a surprisingly simple "story", and (2) this story contradicts a lot of conventional wisdom in optimization.  https://t.co/CWUZPujOTU https://t.co/o8qnBV2qvT

author: zicokolter
text: New paper with @priyald17,  @roderickmelrose, and Mahyar Fazlyab.  Really excited about these directions for integrating robust control into deep RL methods.

quoted.text:
Provable robustness is vital for safety-critical systems like planes/power grids, but deep RL has struggled to provide needed guarantees

Our new #ICLR2021 paper tackles this by fusing robust control & deep RL
